subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — NovaCorp redlines on IP defense and indemnity
content:
--- Message 1 ---
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novacorp.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: customer control of IP defense + carveouts

Ben —

Thanks for taking a look. Attached are NovaCorp's MSA + Order Form redlines (see NovaCorp_MSA_redlines_v2.docx). High level asks: we need the right to control defense of third-party IP claims arising from outputs we receive using Redwood services; broad warranty language around non-infringement of customer data derivatives; and clarity on evidence preservation and cooperation timelines.

Key items we want to get across the line:
- Customer shall have the right to select counsel and control defense for third-party IP claims that arise from our downstream product (we often need to protect product brand).
- Redwood to indemnify for third-party IP claims to the extent caused by Redwood's models or hosted models you provide.
- Narrow exclusions for: (i) claims based on customer modifications, (ii) claims based on open-source components with their own licenses, and (iii) claims arising from customer data we supplied.

We flagged a couple of practical asks: 14-day notice windows, preservation obligations, and proof-of-infringement threshold so we don't end up in speculative litigation. Please review and let us know Redwood's position.

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Director, Contracts & Privacy
NovaCorp

Attachment: NovaCorp_MSA_redlines_v2.docx (docx)

--- Message 2 ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: customer control of IP defense + carveouts

Dana —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline file. I read through and discussed with product/legal this morning. We want to get to a practical compromise quickly so procurement can sign the order form. High level counter-proposal:

1) Defense control: Redwood will retain the right to defend third-party IP claims that stem from the models and model-internal code we provide. However, we are open to granting Customer the right to participate and select outside counsel in limited circumstances (e.g., where Customer integration or branding exposure is material).

2) Indemnity carve: Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims to the extent the claim arises solely from Redwood-provided models or services (not customer customizations or customer data). We want to exclude open-source license claims where liability flows from the OSS upstream obligations.

3) Notice & cooperation: Agreeable to 14-day notice and preservation obligations. We propose a cooperation clause where Customer provides reasonable assistance and Redwood covers reasonable defense costs.

4) Monetary cap: Proposal: indemnity subject to the Order Form financial cap (2x the annual recurring fees for the affected product). Open to discussing higher thresholds for enterprise customers but need procurement signoff.

I've attached a shortone-page summary with suggested inline language (Redwood_proposed_defense_language.pdf). Looping in Marissa (legal) to convert this into redline text and confirm whether mutual defense language or assignable control is acceptable.

Next step: Marissa, can you draft suggested wording that maps to above and highlights where we must push back (e.g., open-source carveouts / cap)?

Thanks — Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_proposed_defense_language.pdf (pdf)

--- Message 3 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: customer control of IP defense + carveouts

Dana / Ben —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed both the NovaCorp redlines and Ben's summary. Below is proposed contract language we think is a commercially balanced compromise — please treat as working text that we can redline back into your document:

"Right to Defend; Control of Defense. Redwood shall have the right, at its sole option, to assume control of the defense and settlement of any third-party claim alleging that the Services or models provided by Redwood infringe or misappropriate a third party's intellectual property rights. Customer may elect to assume control of the defense where Customer demonstrates that (i) the alleged claim arises solely from Customer's product branding or modifications to the Services; or (ii) Customer reasonably demonstrates a material risk to its business brand that cannot be mitigated by participation alone. If Redwood assumes control of the defense, Redwood shall not settle any claim that requires Customer to admit liability, pay money, or take injunctive relief without Customer's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld)."

"Indemnity Scope. Subject to the limitations below, Redwood will indemnify Customer against damages, settlements and reasonable defense costs finally awarded against Customer resulting from third-party claims to the extent they arise from the unmodified Services or models provided by Redwood. Redwood's indemnity shall not apply to claims: (a) arising from Customer's modifications to the Services; (b) based on Customer-provided data or integration; (c) arising from third-party open-source components used by Customer or Customer's own products; or (d) attributable to Customer's negligence or willful misconduct."

"Notice, Cooperation and Mitigation. Customer will notify Redwood promptly (no later than 14 days after receipt of notice) and reasonably cooperate with Redwood in the defense. Redwood will keep Customer reasonably informed and pay reasonable costs of defense. Parties will use good faith efforts to mitigate potential damages."

"Monetary Cap. The indemnity will be subject to the cap in the Order Form (2x ARR for the purchased term), provided that either party may seek a higher cap through procurement approvals and documented exec signoff."

Comments:
- We must keep the open-source carveout (c) as written — exposure there can be pervasive and difficult to insure.
- The settlement consent carve (no admission / injunctive without consent) protects both sides and is standard.
- We recommend adding a short evidence-preservation bullet referencing and pointing to an operational SLO for preservation steps (we can work with Ops to supply a template).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

--- Message 4 ---
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novacorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: customer control of IP defense + carveouts

Ben / Dana —

Quick note from procurement: NovaCorp can live with Redwood-led defense for model-origin claims if Redwood adds reciprocal indemnity for any breach of Customer data that causes third-party claims, and confirms SLAs for evidence preservation (we'll give examples in the procurement checklist). Also need confirmation that the monetary cap can be revisited for material risk (we won't sign if the cap is too low given downstream revenue exposure).

I've attached a short procurement checklist that lists the items our contract team wants visible on the order form.

Tom Reynolds
Senior Procurement Manager
NovaCorp

Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

--- Message 5 ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novacorp.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: customer control of IP defense + carveouts

Tom / Dana —

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic feedback. Redwood legal accepts the approach Marissa outlined with two follow-ups we can live with:
1) Add explicit reciprocal indemnity for breaches of Customer data that cause third-party claims (narrowly scoped to Redwood's systems/security failures).
2) Add an explicit evidence-preservation SOW reference and a 14-day notice + 30-day staging window for evidence handoff; Ops will provide the template.

On monetary cap: Procurement can request a higher cap; our standard for enterprise is to escalate to sales leadership and finance for exceptions. If NovaCorp can provide a short justification (expected downstream revenue tied to the integration), we can fast-track approval.

If that is acceptable, I'll have legal generate a redline and a countersign-ready order form. Can we route the final to the HubSpot deal above and push to DocuSign? I've included the DocuSign link here for convenience: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abcdef123456

Next steps:
- Dana: confirm ability to accept Redwood-driven defense with the reciprocal data indemnity and evidence SOW.
- Tom: confirm approval to route to procurement execs for cap exception if necessary.
- Marissa / Kimberly: produce the redline for signature (we aim to have the countersign-ready packet by EOD Wed).

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
